questions.subject: PCMB & Computer Foundation
questions.question: (Physics) A body of mass $4\text{ kg}$ accelerates at $3\text{ m/s}^2$ under a net force. According to Newton's Second Law ($F = ma$), what is the magnitude of the net force?
questions.hint: Multiply mass in kg by acceleration in m/s^2.
questions.explanation: By Newton's second law of motion, $F = m \cdot a = 4\text{ kg} \times 3\text{ m/s}^2 = 12\text{ N}$.

questions.subject: PCMB & Computer Foundation
questions.question: (Chemistry) At $298\text{ K}$ ($25^\circ\text{C}$), what is the $\text{pH}$ value of pure neutral water?
questions.hint: Neutral point sits cleanly in the middle of the 0–14 pH scale.
questions.explanation: At $298\text{ K}$, pure water has $[\text{H}^+] = [\text{OH}^-] = 10^{-7}\text{ M}$, so $\text{pH} = -\log_{10}(10^{-7}) = 7$.

questions.subject: PCMB & Computer Foundation
questions.question: (Mathematics) What is the discriminant $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac$ and nature of roots for the quadratic equation $x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$?
questions.hint: Compare with $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ where $a=1, b=-5, c=6$.
questions.explanation: $\Delta = (-5)^2 - 4(1)(6) = 25 - 24 = 1 > 0$. Since $\Delta > 0$, the roots ($2$ and $3$) are real and distinct.

questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the cell's supply of ATP via oxidative phosphorylation and possess their own circular DNA and $70\text{S}$ ribosomes.
